     2	 * Pure path-segment validation utilities (no I/O, no storage dependencies).
     3	 *
     4	 * - `assertSafeSegment()` — boolean predicate; validates a single path segment
     5	 *   against `SAFE_SLUG_REGEX` (`/^[a-z0-9][a-z0-9-]*$/`). Used as the canonical
     6	 *   slug-validation delegate by all `assertSafeSlug()` wrappers in the codebase
     7	 *   (storage layer, GUI handlers) and directly by any site that needs to produce
     8	 *   a layer-specific error on rejection.
     9	 * - `planFolderBasename()` — validates the `{YYYY-MM-DD}-{name}` plan-folder
    10	 *   naming convention and returns the folder basename; throws on mismatch.
    11	 * - `validatePlanPath()` — non-throwing wrapper around `planFolderBasename()`.

    13	 * Project-path resolution (`resolveProjectPath`, `formatCandidateList`) lives in

    15	 */

    18	import { SAFE_SLUG_REGEX } from './constants.js';
    19	
    20	// Pattern: YYYY-MM-DD followed by a hyphen and at least one character
    21	// Example: 2026-02-16-technical-debt-cleanup
    22	const planFolderPattern = /^\d{4}-\d{2}-\d{2}-.+$/;
    23	
    24	/**
    25	 * Maximum allowed length (in characters) for a single path segment validated by
    26	 * {@link assertSafeSegment}. Segments exceeding this limit are rejected even when
    27	 * they otherwise satisfy {@link SAFE_SLUG_REGEX}.
    28	 */
    29	export const MAX_SEGMENT_LENGTH = 128;
    30	
    31	/**
    32	 * Returns `true` when `segment` is a valid slug segment (lowercase alphanumeric
    33	 * with hyphens, must start with an alphanumeric character, and at most
    34	 * {@link MAX_SEGMENT_LENGTH} characters long), `false` otherwise.
    35	 *
    36	 * Uses {@link SAFE_SLUG_REGEX} from `constants.ts` — callers are responsible for
    37	 * constructing their own layer-specific errors when this returns `false`.
    38	 *
    39	 * The `Boolean(segment)` guard is intentional defense-in-depth: {@link SAFE_SLUG_REGEX}
    40	 * (`/^[a-z0-9][a-z0-9-]*$/`) already rejects empty strings via its `^[a-z0-9]` anchor,
